sections.title: prepositions of time and place: at, in, on

reference.title: at, in, on
rows: countries and cities: in Spain, in Madrid; rooms: in the kitchen; buildings: in a shop, in a museum; closed spaces: in a park, in a garden, in a car
months: in February, in June; seasons: in (the) winter; years: in 2018; times of day: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening
transport: on a bike, on a bus, on a train, on a plane, on a ship; a surface: on the floor, on a table, on a shelf, on the balcony, on the roof, on the wall
dates: on 1st March; days: on Tuesday, on New Year’s Day, on Valentine’s Day
places: at school, at home, at work, at university, at the airport, at the station, at a bus stop
times: at 6 o’clock, at half past two, at quarter to eight; at night, at the weekend; festival periods: at Christmas, at Easter

reference.title: in the morning, on Monday morning
reference.text: We say in the morning / afternoon / evening, but on + a day + morning / afternoon / evening: on Monday morning, on Friday night. And at night, not in the night.

reference.title: in a car, on a bus
reference.text: Use in with a car or a taxi, but on with a bus, a train, a plane, a ship, or a bike.

reference.wrong: I have an exam in Monday.
reference.right: I have an exam on Monday.

reference.wrong: We never work in the weekend.
reference.right: We never work at the weekend.

reference.why: Years, months, and seasons take in.

reference.wrong: I’ll meet you in the station.
reference.right: I’ll meet you at the station.
reference.why: at for a place where something happens: at the station, at the airport, at a bus stop.

tasks.instruction: Communication: at, in, on. Ask and answer the questions with a preposition and a time or place
tasks.note: SB 2c + Communication 2B (A p.103, B p.109): ученик — A, ИИ — B

exercises.situation: You are a classmate in an English class (level: pre-intermediate), Student B in a pair activity about at, in, on. First the student (Student A) asks you these questions: What month do you usually go on holiday? Where do you usually have breakfast? What time do you usually have lunch? What days of the week do you usually go out in the evening? What time of day do you usually do your English homework? Where do you usually buy clothes? Where do you normally listen to music? When’s your birthday? Answer each one with a short answer with at, in, or on and a time or place (e.g. In August. / In the kitchen. / At about half past one. / On Fridays and Saturdays. / In the evening. / In shops in the city centre. / In the car. / On 12th May.), then ask What about you? Then ask your questions, one at a time: Where were you born? What time do you usually get up during the week? Where do you usually have lunch? What time of day do you usually meet friends? When do you usually go shopping? Where do you usually do your English homework? When do you do housework? Where can you have a nice walk near where you live? If the student uses the wrong preposition (in Monday, at the summer, in the weekend), repeat the phrase correctly in your next reply without a long explanation.
exercises.goal: at, in, on: ask your questions and answer your partner's.
exercises.opener: Hi! Let’s do the at, in, on questions. You start – ask me your first question.
criteria: asks at least five of Student A’s questions correctly (What month do you usually go on holiday? Where do you usually have breakfast? …)
answers with the correct preposition + a time or place (in August, on Saturdays, at 7.30, at home, in the kitchen)
uses at, in, and on each at least once correctly
asks What about you? after answering

reference.title: Past continuous: was / were + verb + -ing
rows: Yes, he was. / No, he wasn’t.
Yes, they were. / No, they weren’t.

reference.text: We use the past continuous to describe an action in progress at a specific moment in the past: At 8.45 last Saturday I was walking in the park. The birds were singing. It wasn’t raining. What were you doing at 11 o’clock last night? I was watching TV. We often use it to describe the situation at the beginning of a story: In 1972 I was living in London.

reference.title: Past simple or past continuous?
rows: We were walking in the gardens when he took a photo of us.
My sister arrived when I was having lunch.

reference.title: Two actions
reference.text: We often use the past continuous and the past simple together in the same sentence. The past continuous is a longer action that was happening in the background when the shorter past simple action happened.

reference.title: Spelling: -ing
reference.text: Most verbs add -ing: work → working. Verbs ending in e: have → having, write → writing. Consonant–vowel–consonant: run → running, stop → stopping. study → studying.

reference.wrong: I was work when you called.
reference.right: I was working when you called.

reference.wrong: When I was arriving, they were having dinner.
reference.right: When I arrived, they were having dinner.
reference.why: The short action that interrupts is in the past simple.

reference.title: Weak forms
reference.text: In positive sentences and wh- questions, was and were are usually unstressed and pronounced /wəz/ and /wə/: I was staying with him. What were you doing? They are stressed in negatives (wasn’t, weren’t) and in short answers (Yes, it was.), and often at the start of a yes / no question (Was it at Kim’s house?).

reference.why: Don’t stress were in a positive sentence.

reference.title: Telling a story about a photo
reference.text: Start with the situation (past continuous): In 1972, I was living in London. Then say what happened (past simple): One night, I went to a nightclub and I met a young Frenchman.

tasks.instruction: Look at the photo by Henri Cartier-Bresson. Then read the article and answer the questions
tasks.note: SB 1a+1b: догадки по фото (1a) проверяются статьёй (1b) → Blank на ключевое слово; фото — из SB p.16. Ответы по тексту статьи (MODEL)
tasks.context:
That’s me in the picture. The Guardian newspaper has a weekly feature called That’s me in the picture, where people describe famous photos they were in. This photo was sent in by Jane Rangeley.

In 1972, I was living in London. I was in my early twenties, and I was working for an advertising agency. That summer, I went on a camping holiday with my parents in the south of France. One night, I went to a nightclub on the beach and I met a young Frenchman, and we fell in love. When I got home, I immediately started looking for a job in Paris. He was at university there – he was studying medicine. In the end, I found a job as a secretary with UNESCO, and I went to live there.

We lived together for six years. On Sundays, we often went for a walk, and one of our favourite places was the botanical gardens. It had a zoo, and I often put some bread in my pocket to give to the animals. We were walking in the gardens one Sunday in autumn when we stopped because a lot of noise was coming from one of the trees. There was an owl there, maybe escaped from the zoo, and some little birds were attacking it. I also noticed a man with a camera. When we started walking again, I said ‘Why was that man taking photographs of us?’.

I now know that Cartier-Bresson often waited in parks in Paris for the perfect photo opportunity. The following year, one of my boyfriend’s friends saw the photo in a magazine. Before I returned to London, I phoned the magazine and I got Cartier-Bresson’s phone number. I was very shy, but I called him. He was very friendly, and he sent me a copy. Years later I met him and he signed the photo for me.

I love this picture. It was a happy time for me. And although my French boyfriend and I broke up in the end, we’re still in touch.

tasks.instruction: Talk to a partner about photos. Give more information if you can
tasks.note: SB 5a → разговор с ИИ

exercises.situation: You are a classmate in an English class (level: pre-intermediate). You and the student talk about photos. Ask these questions one at a time and ask a follow-up question when you can: Do you post photos on social media sites like Instagram or Facebook? What kind of photos do you post? (If not, how do you share photos with friends and family?) Do you have a photo as a background on your phone, tablet, or computer? Who or what is it of? What’s the story behind it? Do you have any photos you really like on your phone? What was happening at the time? Do you have a favourite photo of yourself as a child? Who took it? What were you wearing? Is there a story behind it? When the student asks you, answer too: your phone background is a photo of your dog on the beach in Cornwall – you took it last summer when you were walking there with your brother; your favourite photo as a child: you were five, you were wearing a big red hat, and your grandmother took it at your birthday party. Use the past continuous and the past simple naturally. If the student makes a mistake with the past continuous (e.g. I was wear), repeat it correctly in your reply.
exercises.opener: Hi! Let’s talk about photos. Do you post photos on social media, like Instagram or Facebook?
criteria: answers at least three of the four questions with more information
describes what was happening in a photo with the past continuous (We were walking…, I was wearing…)
uses the past simple for finished actions (My dad took it…)
asks the partner at least one question back

steps.text: Say if you post photos on social media
steps.example: Yes, I post photos on Instagram, usually of food and places.

steps.text: Talk about the background on your phone
steps.example: My background is a photo of my cat. She was sleeping on the sofa.

steps.text: Describe a photo you really like
steps.example: I really like a photo from the mountains. We were walking and it was snowing.

steps.text: Describe a photo of you as a child
steps.example: My dad took it when I was six. I was wearing a funny hat.

steps.text: Ask your classmate a question back
steps.example: What about you? Who took your favourite photo?

tasks.instruction: Match the questions to paragraphs 1–3. Write the number of the paragraph
tasks.note: Writing 2b; пункты без номеров в книге → n по порядку. Ответы MODEL
tasks.context:
1 This is one of my favourite photos. It’s of two storks. I took the photo in the spring of 2018 when I was on holiday with some friends in Andalucia, in the south of Spain, at a place called Doñana National Park.
2 Doñana is a nature reserve which is famous because there are lots of wonderful birds there, like storks and flamingos. Storks are my favourite birds in the world because they’re big birds, but they’re very elegant. I love taking photos of animals and birds, but I’m not very good at it! Here I was learning how to use the zoom on my new camera, because the storks were quite far away from us on the top of a tree. I needed to keep very still because I didn’t want to frighten them, but for the first time I got a really good close-up shot.
3 I love this photo because it was my first successful wildlife photo, and the blue sky reminds me of the wonderful weather in Andalucia. I have it on my phone and as the background on my laptop.
